Simulate repeated MFO tests with a known truth

Source: R/simulate_MFO_sessions.R
simulate_MFO_sessions.Rd

Generates synthetic MFO tests (resting measure, MFO test and graded test) for several participants and sessions, with known true MFO, Fatmax and SIN parameters. It is meant for testing the reliability (SPEC 12) and uncertainty (SPEC 13) modules and for demonstrations, not as a model of physiology.

Usage

simulate_MFO_sessions(
  n_participants = 10,
  n_sessions = 2,
  population,
  shape = "basic",
  cv_MFO = 0.21,
  cv_Fatmax = 0.26,
  familiarization = 0,
  noise_cv = 0,
  noise_cor = 0,
  fat_noise_cv = 0,
  protocol = MFO_protocol(),
  n_steps = 8,
  intensity = c(20, 75),
  step_time = 20,
  author = c("Frayn", "Jeukendrup", "Peronnet"),
  hr_rest = 60,
  age = 30,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n_participants

number of participants.

n_sessions

number of sessions per participant.

population

list with `VO2max` (mean and SD, mL/min; required) and optionally `MFO` (g/min) and `Fatmax` (% VO2max), each `c(mean, sd)`. An SD of 0 gives the same value to every participant.

shape

`"basic"` (d = 0, s = 1; default), `"trained"` (d = 0.18, s = 1.52, the trained participant of Cheneviere et al. 2009, Fig. 5), or a list with `d` and `s`, each one number or one per participant.

cv_MFO, cv_Fatmax

between-session coefficients of variation (proportions; defaults 0.21 and 0.26).

familiarization

relative bias of session 1, one number for MFO and Fatmax or `c(MFO = , Fatmax = )` (default 0).

noise_cv, noise_cor

analyser noise per record: coefficient of variation of VO2 and VCO2 and their correlation (defaults 0).

fat_noise_cv

error of the FAT of each step around the true curve, as a proportion of MFO (default 0).

protocol

an [MFO_protocol()] of type `"step"`, `"step_variable"` or `"relative"`.

n_steps

number of exercise steps (default 8).

intensity

% VO2max of the first and last step (default 20 and 75).

step_time

record interval in seconds (default 20); step durations and the averaged segment must be multiples of it.

author

equation whose inverse gives VCO2: "Frayn" (default), "Jeukendrup" or "Peronnet". Analyse the data with the same `author` to recover the truth.

hr_rest, age

resting heart rate (bpm) and age (years) for the heart-rate line (defaults 60 and 30).

seed

optional integer for reproducible results; the random state of the session is restored afterwards.

Value

An object of class `MFO_sim`: a list with

  • `data`: `data$P01$S1` is a list with `db_basal`, `db_MFO` and `db_graded`, ready for [MFO()] with `step_time`;

  • `truth`: one row per participant and session with `id`, `session`, `VO2max`, `MFO`, `Fatmax`, `d`, `s`, `t` and `Fatmin` (second zero of the SIN curve);

  • `participants`: the participants' values before the between-session variation;

  • `settings`: the arguments, including `step_time` and `protocol`.

Details

**How a test is built.** Each participant has a true VO2max, MFO and curve shape. Fat oxidation follows the SIN model of Cheneviere et al. (2009, doi:10.1249/MSS.0b013e31819e2f91 ), FAT = MFO x SIN(x; d, s, t), truncated at 0, with x the step intensity (% VO2max); t is set so that the maximum falls at the participant's Fatmax. Each step has VO2 = x / 100 x VO2max and the VCO2 for which the `author` equation gives that FAT, so [MFO()] recovers the curve exactly when there is no noise. VO2 is constant within a step (no on-kinetics). Steps are cut as in `protocol`, which also gives the load schedule (`Load` column only when `load_start` and `load_increment` are set).

**Variability.** Three levels:

  • between participants: MFO (log-normal), Fatmax (normal, truncated to `intensity`) and VO2max (normal, positive) from `population`. The MFO and Fatmax defaults are the sedentary adults of Amaro-Gahete, Sanchez-Delgado and Ruiz (2018): 0.34 +/- 0.10 g/min and 44.2 +/- 12.4 % VO2max. VO2max has no default and must be given.

  • between sessions: each session multiplies the participant's MFO and Fatmax by log-normal factors with coefficients of variation `cv_MFO` and `cv_Fatmax`. The defaults, 21 % and 26 %, are the total test-retest CVs reported by Chrzanowski-Smith et al. (2020, n = 99), which include biological, analyser and fitting error; used here as day-to-day variation, and with analyser noise on top, they make the simulated test-retest variability an upper bound. For Fatmax, Croci et al. (2014, n = 15) report CVs of 16.4 % (SIN), 18.6 % (P3) and 20.8 % (MV). `familiarization` shifts session 1 only (a relative bias).

  • within a session, on fat oxidation: `fat_noise_cv` adds to the true FAT of each step a normal error with standard deviation `fat_noise_cv` x MFO (the CV of the step FAT around the true curve, residual SD / MFO; SPEC 17). VCO2 is then solved from the noisy FAT, so [MFO()] sees exactly that error.

  • within a session, on the gases: every record of VO2 and VCO2 is multiplied by (1 + e), with e normal, standard deviation `noise_cv` and correlation `noise_cor` between the two gases. Small errors in the gases become large errors in FAT, which depends on their difference; there is no source for a realistic correlation, so `noise_cor` defaults to 0.

Both noises default to 0 (noiseless tests); studies of the fit uncertainty set them explicitly as design parameters.

**Resting and graded tests.** Conveniences for [MFO()], not physiological claims: the resting measure lasts 15 min at 10 % VO2max with RER 0.80; the graded test has 60-s stages from 50 to 100 % VO2max with RER rising linearly from 0.90 to 1.15, so the last stage gives VO2max exactly. Heart rate rises linearly with % VO2max from `hr_rest` to the predicted HRmax of Tanaka, Monahan and Seals (2001, doi:10.1016/s0735-1097(00)01054-8 ), 208 - 0.7 x `age`.

References

Amaro-Gahete FJ, Sanchez-Delgado G, Ruiz JR (2018). Commentary: Contextualising maximal fat oxidation during exercise: determinants and normative values. Front Physiol 9: 1460, Table 1 (sedentary adults). doi:10.3389/fphys.2018.01460

Chrzanowski-Smith OJ, Edinburgh RM, Thomas MP, et al. (2020). The day-to-day reliability of peak fat oxidation and FATMAX. Eur J Appl Physiol 120: 1745-1759. doi:10.1007/s00421-020-04397-3

Croci I, Borrani F, Byrne NM, et al. (2014). Reproducibility of Fatmax and fat oxidation rates during exercise in recreationally trained males. PLoS ONE 9: e97930. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0097930

See also

[write_MFO_sessions()], [MFO()], [MFO_kinetics()]

Examples

sim <- simulate_MFO_sessions(n_participants = 3, n_sessions = 2,
                             population = list(VO2max = c(3000, 500)),
                             seed = 1)
sim
#> <MFO_sim> 3 participant(s) x 2 session(s), 8 steps of step, 20-s records (Frayn)
#>   between sessions: CV MFO 0.21, CV Fatmax 0.26; familiarization MFO 0, Fatmax 0
#>   noise: FAT CV 0 of MFO; gases CV 0, correlation 0
#>   true MFO 0.222-0.548 g/min, Fatmax 41.5-71.6 % VO2max
sim$truth
#>    id session   VO2max       MFO   Fatmax d s           t    Fatmin
#> 1 P01      S1 2686.773 0.4743505 71.58174 0 1 -0.67801032 121.58174
#> 2 P01      S2 2686.773 0.5480535 41.48361 0 1  0.26755014  91.48361
#> 3 P02      S1 3091.822 0.2215653 68.85326 0 1 -0.59229272 118.85326
#> 4 P02      S2 3091.822 0.3477422 51.42501 0 1 -0.04476787 101.42501
#> 5 P03      S1 2582.186 0.3066262 61.30081 0 1 -0.35502533 111.30081
#> 6 P03      S2 2582.186 0.2851269 62.85278 0 1 -0.40378191 112.85278
s1 <- sim$data$P01$S1
r <- MFO(step_time = sim$settings$step_time, db_MFO = s1$db_MFO,
         db_basal = s1$db_basal, db_graded = s1$db_graded, cv_var = "RER",
         author = "Frayn", energy_equivalents = "classic", age = 30)
#> VO2max: a 30-s window is not a multiple of step_time (20 s); using 2 record(s) = 40 s.
c(estimated = r$FAT_MAX, true = sim$truth$Fatmax[1])
#> estimated      true 
#>  70.41290  71.58174
